title: Benchmarking Hybrid Deep Learning Architectures for Predictive Maintenance in Industry 4.0
abstract: arXiv:2609.22583v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: Predictive maintenance in Industry 4.0 refers to using data from sensors, machines, and production systems to estimate when equipment is likely to fail, so maintenance can be planned before a breakdown occurs [1]. However, a model that predicts maintenance may work perfectly in the lab but fail unexpectedly when applied to real factory data [2]. To solve this "reliability" gap, we evaluated six deep learning architectures across more than 700 experimental runs. We focused on the two dominant approaches in the field: Recurrent Neural Networks (RNNs), which process data step-by-step, like reading a sentence [3], and Transformers, a recent dominant approach, which look at the entire sequence at once to spot important connections [4]. translated_abstract: 工业4.0中的预测性维护是指利用传感器、机器和生产系统的数据来估计设备何时可能发生故障，从而在故障发生之前规划维护工作。然而，一个预测维护的模型可能在实验室中表现完美，但在应用于真实工厂数据时却意外失效。为解决这一“可靠性”差距，我们在超过700次实验运行中评估了六种深度学习架构。我们重点关注了该领域的两种主流方法：循环神经网络（RNN），它像阅读句子一样逐步处理数据；以及Transformer——一种近期占主导地位的方法，它一次性查看整个序列以发现重要关联。我们研究了当数据包含噪声时，Transformer是否仍然优于循环神经网络（RNN）。我们发现，虽然Transformer擅长跟踪稳定、缓慢变化的过程，但它们（摘要在此处截断）
tldr: 该论文通过超过700次实验的系统基准测试，比较了RNN和Transformer等六种深度学习架构在工业4.0预测性维护任务中的可靠性，发现Transformer虽擅长跟踪稳定缓慢的过程，但在含噪声的真实工厂数据中面临可靠性挑战。
en_tdlr: This paper benchmarks six deep learning architectures, including RNNs and Transformers, across 700+ experimental runs for predictive maintenance in Industry 4.0, finding that while Transformers excel at tracking stable, slow-moving processes, they face reliability challenges when applied to noisy real-world factory data.
